subject.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)

question: Should Telegram final-mode TTS opt into the new public `captionedFinalText` channel capability by default, making one captioned voice note the normal result while separate text-plus-voice remains a distinct product request?
rationale: The implementation is a plausible architecture-aligned bug fix, but it creates a public plugin contract and selects a Telegram delivery default that conflicts with a documented preference for separate messages; automation cannot choose that permanent API and UX policy.

options.title: Approve capability and default
options.body: Accept the generic SDK capability and Telegram opt-in, then require exact-head Telegram proof before merge.

options.title: Keep the seam private
options.body: Narrow the repair to an internal Telegram-aware capability path and defer the third-party SDK contract until another channel needs it.

options.title: Pause for delivery-mode design
options.body: Coordinate with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42539 and design an explicit bundled-versus-separate product policy before landing this behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve capability and default
recommendation.body: Accept the generic SDK capability and Telegram opt-in, then require exact-head Telegram proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history connects this person most broadly to ACP finalization, channel capability registration, and plugin SDK architecture, which are the decision surfaces here.
